title: You weren’t just hesitating.
paragraphs:
You weren’t just hesitating.
You were negotiating with the very thing God already decided about you.

You keep replaying it—
that moment when you knew you should step forward, speak up, obey…
and instead, you built a case for why you couldn’t.

It sounded reasonable.
It felt safe.
It looked like wisdom.
But it was an excuse.
And you’re not the first to do it.

There was a man standing in front of a burning bush—fire that didn’t consume, a voice that didn’t stutter, a calling that didn’t ask permission.
That man was Moses.
And what he said next sounds uncomfortably familiar.
“Who am I that I should go…?” (Book of Exodus 3:11)
Read that again.

Not “What do You want me to do, Lord?”
Not “How will You do it through me?”
But—
Who am I?

That wasn’t humility.
It was limitation disguised as humility.
Because buried inside that question was a quiet refusal:
“I don’t see myself the way You see me.”
And that’s where excuses are born.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.

Moses had history.
Failure.
A past he couldn’t erase.
A reputation he couldn’t outrun.
He had already tried once—and failed publicly.

So when God called him again, he didn’t say no outright.
He just… stalled.

First it was identity: “Who am I?”
Then it became doubt: “What if they don’t believe me?”
Then insecurity: “I’m not eloquent…”
Then finally, honesty slipped out: “Please send someone else.”
That’s how excuses evolve.

They rarely start as rebellion.
They start as self-protection.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Every excuse you give God is rooted in one assumption:
That your limitation is stronger than His authority.

God didn’t answer Moses by fixing his résumé.
He didn’t boost his confidence.
He didn’t list his qualifications.
He said something far more dangerous—
“I will be with you.” (Exodus 3:12)
That’s it.

Because the calling was never about Moses’ ability.
It was about God’s presence.
And that changes everything.

You keep waiting to feel ready.
You keep asking for clarity, confidence, confirmation.
But what if the delay isn’t because God hasn’t spoken—
What if it’s because you’re still negotiating with what He already said?

God saw it.
That moment you chose comfort over obedience.
That opportunity you buried under “I’m not ready yet.”
That nudge you silenced with logic.
You knew.

Excuses don’t just delay obedience.
They reshape destiny.

Israel stayed in bondage longer because Moses argued.
Purpose paused because fear spoke louder than faith.
And before you try to soften that truth—
Look at your own life.

How many doors stayed closed because you convinced yourself you weren’t “that kind of person”?
How many callings felt distant not because God withdrew…
but because you stepped back?
There are two versions of your future forming right now.

One where you keep explaining yourself out of obedience—
refining your excuses, perfecting your delays, mastering avoidance.
And another—

Where you step into something you don’t feel qualified for…
and discover God was never waiting for your ability in the first place.
That tension you feel?
That’s not pressure.
That’s invitation.

The Gospel doesn’t call the qualified.
It qualifies the called.
Because the same pattern you see in Moses points forward to Jesus Christ.

Where Moses hesitated, Jesus obeyed fully.
Where Moses questioned identity, Jesus declared it.
Where Moses asked “Who am I?”—
Jesus said, “I AM.”
And then He went to the cross for people who keep making excuses.

“For all have sinned…” (Romans 3:23)
That includes the moments you chose comfort over calling.
But it doesn’t end there.
“…while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

Grace doesn’t wait for your readiness.
It meets you in your resistance.

And redemption doesn’t erase your past—
it repurposes it.

Moses became the very leader he thought he could never be.
Not because he overcame his weakness—
But because he stopped letting it define him.
So here you are.
Still thinking about that thing you’ve been avoiding.

Still rehearsing reasons.
Still managing fear.
But something inside you knows—
This isn’t about capability anymore.
It’s about surrender.
Say it.
“I’ve been making excuses.”

Not for shame—
but for freedom.

Because the moment you stop defending your limitation…
is the moment God starts rewriting your direction.

Stay close to this kind of truth.
Not the comfortable version.
The one that confronts you and calls you higher.
There’s more depth waiting—Scripture unpacked, patterns exposed, real transformation, not surface motivation.
And don’t keep this to yourself.

Someone in your life is stuck in the same cycle—
thinking they’re being wise, when they’re actually being held back.

Send this to them.
Not to call them out—
But to call them forward.
Follow this journey if you’re done playing safe with your calling.
Because it will.
And when it does—
Remember Moses.
And remember what God said anyway.
